title: Ordinary finiteness of four closed dualizing inputs
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $D$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $1\le m\le n$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ with the fixed universe lifts and quotient homomorphism [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility]. For a closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A_k^r$ with affine $Y$, let $I_R$ be the right adjoint of the actual identity-open compact support at $i$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Put $M=\omega_{P,A}$, $N=I_AM$, and $M_B=T_PM$. Then $M,N,M_B,I_BM_B$ are all bounded constructible with an ordered finite Tor interval, tested against every degree-zero sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude].

source.place: Paragraph 3: ordinary dualizing objects for a closed affine embedding and site realization

proof.text: Construct omega_P,R and omega_Y,R at both positive levels by coefDualizingConstruction; their ordinary finiteness is part of its conclusion. The closed immersion is proper, so identity-open compact support is closed direct image. Its right adjoint preserves bounded-below objects on the quasi-compact target.

Compact-support composition and the two ordinary adjunctions give the same represented Hom functor for I_R omega_P,R and omega_Y,R on D+. The representing-object normalization identifies them by a counit-compatible isomorphism. Transfer bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude, proving the clause for N.

Affine dualizing coefficient reduction identifies T_P omega_P,A with omega_P,B. The fixed scalar extension is canonically identified with the ordinary scalar extension by uniqueness of its left adjoint. Apply I_B, then the preceding composition identification, and transport finiteness. This also works for empty Y, and m=n, without finite Tor dimension of B over A.
